label: rejected

evidence.V1: The front, three-quarter and silhouette clearly read as a standing banner on a pole, and the top view shows the bar, finial and base disc.
evidence.V2: Clear tiers: cloth and pole (big), base disc and crossbar (medium), finial balls, end knobs, top band and emblem (small).
evidence.V3: The cloth is a perfectly flat rigid rectangle with no folds, sway or tail cut, and the emblem is an ambiguous notched shape that reads as a cursor arrow in the three-quarter view, so the stylisation is only partial.
evidence.V4: Base and bar are rounded, but the cloth panel has thin hard edges and a square bottom with no softening, so edge treatment is inconsistent.
evidence.V5: Close-finial studio shows visible low-poly faceting on the gold sphere, and the cloth/emblem are clean otherwise. Minor.
evidence.V6: One cloth hue in 2 values (body plus darker top band), wood pole, gold fittings and an ink base rim. Disciplined, and the crimson and shadow colourways hold.
evidence.V7: 956 tris against a medium target of 2000, so it is under target.
evidence.V8: Gold #E8AE38-style fittings, ink base and single vertex-colour material match, but the faceted finial sphere and flat unchamfered cloth card are slightly off the smooth, chamfered kit look.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Anchored, Box fidelity, CanTouch off, Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin bottom-centre. A15 X error 0.0, emblem offset 0.0. Correct.

top_fixes: Give the cloth gentle vertical folds and a shaped tail (swallowtail or pointed) so it reads as fabric, not a board
Replace the emblem with a clearly readable symbol (star, crest, crown) that does not look like an arrow cursor
Add segments or weighted normals to the finial spheres and a small chamfer on the cloth edges
